LanguageData.BOR_KwazaarBazaar.label: kwazaar bazaar
LanguageData.BOR_KwazaarBazaar.description:
Nobody calls them the Kwazaar Bazaar to their face. The name belongs to outsiders — travelers who learned to approach their stations carefully and leave with their inventories intact, if they were fortunate. The Kwazaari themselves use a simpler term: humans. The word implies everything you need to know about how they regard the rest of settled space.
They are, by most historical accounts, closer to the original Solarite bloodline than the republics that claim the name. They do not care. The past stopped being useful a long time ago, and the Kwazaari are very particular about what counts as currency.
The warring monkeys below them can either be useful or used. Kwazaari isolate themselves and trading with them requires paying them a few favours first.
The Kwazaari don't really care about trade, they are extremely self-sufficient. They are more interested in gathering information and keeping tabs on the rest of the world, and they have a lot of it. They are also very good at keeping secrets, so it's hard to know how much they actually know.
Their isolationism comes about from the disastrous wars of the past. They are the Solarites that survived the Mechanoid massacres, and they have no interest in repeating that experience. They are also very wary of outsiders, and they have a lot of reasons to be. They are not interested in expanding their territory or their influence, they just want to survive and thrive in their own little corner of the world.
LanguageData.BOR_SolarRepublic.label: solar republic
LanguageData.BOR_SolarRepublic.description:
The Solar Republic is a recurring claim — scattered polities that rediscovered or reconstructed solar-tier technology and wrapped it in the iconography of the old civilization. The framing was pragmatic at first. Over generations it hardened into something closer to faith, and most Solarites today would find it genuinely difficult to say where performance ends and belief begins.
They tend to view their neighbors as people who haven't gotten there yet.
For better or worse. Some of these republics tend to be very dictatorial and war-like; others: charitable and well-meaning. The common thread is that they all have a lot of solar-tier tech, and they all have a lot of pride in it. They are also very competitive with each other, and they are always trying to one-up each other with new inventions and new ways to use their technology.
They really like to show their tech off. Their armors are often very flashy and ornate, and they have a lot of different types of weapons and gadgets that they use to impress each other. They also have a lot of different types of vehicles and ships that they use to show off their technology.
